Lead story · UI / UX · Apple · 3 Nov

Apple splits Health into today and the long run

The iOS 27.3 beta brings back the all-new Health app that Apple tested and then pulled from the iOS 27.2 beta. The big idea is simple: show people how they are doing today on one tab, and how they are changing over the years on another.

Today: Insights. The Insights tab sums up heart, sleep, readiness, fitness, vitals and cycle data through the day. Key numbers sit on cards at the top, with short explanations and graphs below. A "For You" section suggests small changes, such as a new wind-down routine after a few nights of broken sleep.

Over years: Longevity. This tab looks at long-term records across seven areas: heart, sleep, mental wellbeing, movement, metabolic health, hearing and nutrition. Each has its own colour and icon, placed in a ring so you see the whole picture at once. A "Health Age" figure compares Apple Watch data with your real age.

Tests at home. Using the iPhone camera and Apple Watch, people can check flexibility, strength, balance and VO2 max, with live voice and on-screen feedback. Apple says the analysis runs on the device and no video is recorded or stored.

When. The beta reached developers on 3 November. 9to5Mac reports the new app will ship to all users next month, in English, Chinese, French, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Vietnamese and more.

What this means for you

Apple did not just add features; it sorted them by time. That is a lesson for any dashboard you design: ask "when will people look at this?" Put the daily check in one place and the slow trend in another, give each group a fixed colour, and pair every number with one line that explains it.

AI Desk

Higgsfield · Comics · 3 Nov

Higgsfield launches Mangaka for AI comics

The new Mangaka tool turns an idea or a script into a manga, comic or webtoon. It creates characters, locations and chapters (4 to 30, of about 20 to 40 pages each) in one of 14 languages, and exports PDF, CBZ or PNG pages.

Typography · 3 Nov

The brush font that gives AI posters away

Creative Bloq says one look now marks AI-made posters in cafés and village halls: shouty, slanted brush-stroke capitals. Small businesses use it because it is fast and free. It is not even a real font, just lettering the models learned from loud ads and thumbnails. Clients who want to look human will need you.

OpenAI · Product design · 3 Nov

OpenAI says its AI designed a device in a week

OpenAI's hardware team says GPT-6 Astra designed a small device for talking to its Codex agent as a side project in under a week, handling steps from the case design to the circuit board. Its teams now use AI for CAD models and drawings.

Prompt of the day · Test it, score it, then redesign it

The Diwali Gift-Wrap Pattern

Diwali is on Sunday, and every gift needs paper. Today's brief is surface pattern design: one square, seamless repeat tile for "KAAGAZ WRAPS", an invented gift-paper brand. Repeats are hard for AI because the edges must meet perfectly. Try all four versions, tile the result 2 × 2, then score it.

Score: 0 / 5

Student task: rebuild the best tile as vectors in Affinity or Figma, check the repeat at 2 × 2, then wrap a real box with an A4 print. Post the flat tile and the wrapped box side by side.

Version 1 · Any tool
Seamless repeat pattern tile, square 1:1, for Diwali gift-wrapping paper. Flat screen-print style. Deep maroon background. Only four motifs, evenly spaced in a half-drop repeat: a clay diya with one flame, a round marigold flower, a hanging akash kandil lantern, and a small dot rangoli. Only three colours: maroon, saffron and cream. Motifs that touch the edges must continue on the opposite edge. No text, no glitter, no shadows, no 3D.

Why it works: it names the repeat type (half-drop), caps the motifs and colours, and states the edge rule, so each check has one clear answer.

Version 2 · Midjourney V8
flat screen-printed gift wrap pattern, clay diya with single flame, round marigold, hanging akash kandil lantern, dot rangoli, half-drop repeat, deep maroon background, saffron and cream only, generous spacing, Indian festive textile print, no text --tile --ar 1:1 --stylize 150 --no glitter, gold foil, shadows, people, letters

V8 tip: --tile makes the edges wrap. Still test it: open the image four times in a 2 × 2 grid and look for half-cut marigolds at the joins.

Version 3 · Nano Banana
Step 1: Create a square seamless pattern tile for Diwali gift paper. Flat print style, deep maroon background. Use only four motifs, evenly spaced: a clay diya with one flame, a round marigold, a hanging akash kandil and a small dot rangoli. Only maroon, saffron and cream. No text, no shadows.

Step 2 (same chat): Keep the motifs, colours and spacing exactly the same. Make the tile wrap seamlessly: anything cut at the right edge must continue at the left edge, and top must match bottom.

What you are testing: whether the step-2 fix adds a fifth motif, a new colour or a second flame while it repairs the edges.

Version 4 · ChatGPT
Create a 1:1 seamless pattern tile for "KAAGAZ WRAPS", an invented gift-paper brand. Do not show the brand name.

Layout:
1. Background: flat deep maroon
2. Grid: half-drop repeat, 3 rows
3. Motifs, alternating: clay diya (one flame), round marigold, hanging akash kandil, small dot rangoli
4. Colours: saffron and cream only
5. Edges: motifs cut at one edge continue on the opposite edge

Flat print. No text, glitter, shadows or 3D.

Tip: if the edges don't match, reply "shift the tile by half its width and fix only the seam", then ask for a matching gift tag in the same palette.

Graphic Design

Studio rebrand · KISS · 3 Nov

A UK studio makes Cupid its brand

Brand studio KISS rebuilt itself around the line "Brands that Kiss", with a Cupid mascot called Roger Bowman at the centre. The character went through more than 100 form tests. The script wordmark was hand-drawn over about a month: the K and i cross like a heart or a bow, and a line through the letters is the arrow. That arrow line then runs through the whole layout system.

Identity · London Film School · 2 Nov

A film school frames itself in red

Rabbit Hole kept the red the London Film School has used since the 1960s, also seen on its front doors, and only made it brighter for screens. Red frames around the logo and photos stand for choosing what goes inside a film shot. Narrow, bold Waldenburg type runs from big titles down to small details.

Crest · Newcastle United · 3 Nov

Fans vote to refine a crest, not replace it

FutureBrand redrew the 1988 crest after the old details broke down on phones, TV graphics and embroidery. The seahorses, castle and ribbon got cleaner lines and better balance. After two years of fan workshops and surveys, 27,348 fans voted, and 64.8% chose the winning version. It arrives on kits in 2027/28.

UI / UX

Browser · Safari · 3 Nov

Safari adds vertical tabs and dark mode for any site

The iOS, iPadOS and macOS 27.3 betas let Safari show tabs down the left side, as icons by default, with a bar you can widen to see page titles. A new Adaptive Dark Mode offers a "Try" button on sites without a dark theme and builds one for you. Siri can also sort and close tabs. If your site has no dark mode, Safari can now make one for your visitors.

Android · Google Messages · 3 Nov

Google Messages lifts pinned chats and floats search

A beta test moves pinned chats into big contact photos above the chat list, like iMessage, but without last-message previews. Search becomes a floating pill button next to "Start chat" that swaps shape as you scroll, so it stays within thumb reach. The trade-off: favourites become easier to tap but tell you less.

Collaboration · Figma · 1–8 Nov

FigJam lets your cursor pick a character

For a Sanrio birthday tie-up, FigJam users can pick one of 12 characters from a ribbon icon in the toolbar until 8 November. The choice changes the colour of the cursor, tape and sticky notes together. Figma's team turned the original art into resizable vectors and even named colours after each character's habits.

Student Corner

Learning · AAAI · 3 Nov

Ad body plans a 2-day AI bootcamp in Mumbai

The Indie Council of the Advertising Agencies Association of India will run a hands-on AI bootcamp on 20 and 21 November for people at small and independent agencies. It covers AI for strategy, ideas, copy, media, production and pitches. Only 30 seats, first come first served, each session with two teachers, and a certificate at the end.

Reading pick · PRINT · 26 Oct

Your camera roll can become a zine

After losing his job, Samuel Williams went through ten years of phone photos and turned his pictures of hand-made shop signs into a zine, "We Now Copy All Fobs". PRINT's interview shows how an everyday habit of noticing things can become a finished, portfolio-ready project. Look through your own photos tonight.

Design psychology term of the day

Progressive disclosure

Show only what people need now, and keep the detail one step away. It lowers mental load and helps beginners without hiding power from experts. Apple Health puts today's summary first and long-term trends on a separate tab; Safari keeps vertical tabs as icons until you widen the bar.

Try it: take one busy screen from your project. Keep the three things most people need, move the rest behind a "More" or a second tab, and test whether people finish faster.

Indian Design Watch

Design in India
Identity · Indian Garage · 2 Nov

Indian Garage drops "Co" in a rebrand

The homegrown menswear brand from TMRW has a shorter name, a refreshed logo and a new visual identity built around the "Everyday Hero", the self-made young Indian man. The name's idea: many self-made stories start in a garage.

Interactive · Pulse Candy · 3 Nov

A candy game you play with your body

For National Candy Day, DS Group's Pulse launched a 60-second space game that uses the phone camera to track your movements and gestures. Players grab Pulse candies and dodge decoys and asteroids. It runs from 3 to 10 November.

New campaigns
M N Rao · The Content Theory · 3 Nov

"Story of An Indian Tailor"

A documentary-style film marks 60 years of the Mumbai bespoke tailor, using archive photos, old tools and handwritten measurement books. It also flags that fewer young people are learning the craft. Lesson: real archives make a brand film feel honest.

zingbus · 3 Nov

"No Need for Speed"

The intercity bus platform turns its 80 km/h speed lock into the message for festive travel: arriving safely matters more than arriving fast. It runs as a year-round push on social media with travel creators. A rule becomes the idea.

Agency news & awards
Ranking · Havas Media India · 3 Nov

Havas Media India tops RECMA's 2026 rankings

Havas Media India is No. 1 in RECMA's 2026 India qualitative assessment with 21 points and a "Dominant" profile for the fifth year running. It also ranked first for new business from August 2025 to August 2026.

Account win · Hypothesis · 3 Nov

OML's Hypothesis wins nine Wipro brands

Wipro Consumer Care picked Hypothesis, the creator marketing agency from Only Much Louder, for social media and influencer work on nine brands, including Chandrika, Glucovita, Safewash and Softouch, covering content, social and creators.
